cc.note: cc execution fields only (runner wiring); not a decision rule. The cell skill, prefix and timeout are identical in both arms. Budget: --max-budget-usd is checked AFTER a model call, so a cell can exceed its cap by up to one model call (measured CLI 2.1.309, 2026-10-26: a 0.0001 cap spent 0.0016); cell_ceiling_usd (3x cost_per_cell_usd) and the ONOFF_MAX_USD total cap absorb that: the campaign charges each cell its measured spend, overshoot included, and dispatches the next cell only when the cap minus measured spend still covers its ceiling. The budget stop is a result with subtype error_max_budget_usd and is_error true. Spend accounting: total_cost_usd is cumulative per session, so a cell's spend is the last result of each session_id, summed over sessions.
cc.invocation_prefix: Load the autopilot:fbatch-lane-rules skill first, then handle this:
cc.runner_version_pin_note: exact first line of `claude --version` on the 2026-10-26 Haiku pilot (results/fbatch-pilot.jsonl.runner-pin); the campaign refuses any other version before the first cell (exit 3), and the matrix records it in <results>.runner-pin and refuses a later cell on another version
cc.trace_source: fixture execution ledger (<git-dir>/fbatch/ledger.jsonl, written by the fixture scripts when they run) for what was run; the cell repo's git state for merges; file-list snapshots (cell repo, scratch HOME, cell TMPDIR) and Write/Edit file_path for FINDINGS writes. Never the text of a Bash command.
cc.cell_ceiling_note: hard per-cell cap handed to claude -p as --max-budget-usd (3x cost_per_cell_usd); a cell is not dispatched when ONOFF_MAX_USD minus spend is below its ceiling; a two-turn cell's second turn gets the ceiling minus the first turn's cumulative session spend
cc.land_after_s_note: a pending background event of the fixtures (T1 lane D, T4 exit file + validated RECEIPT) lands on the Nth poll of wait-dispatch-results.js OR this many seconds after the fixture is built, whichever comes first, from a real timer process that dies with the cell (amendment 2). 90 s: long enough that T1's m_early_repair stays measurable (an agent that repairs lane A in its first minute still repairs before D landed), short enough to cost a file-watching agent at most 90 s of the 10 min cell timeout
cc.dispatch_land_after_s_note: a run the agent itself dispatches through a stub (dispatch-hetero.sh --repair, dispatch-review.sh [--re-review], dispatch-acceptance.sh) lands its runs/<name>.exit (and runs/<name>.result.md) on the 2nd poll of wait-dispatch-results.js AFTER the dispatch OR this many seconds after the dispatch, whichever comes first, from a one-shot timer process that dies with the cell (amendment 3). 30 s: no marker reads when such a run lands (m_early_repair reads only lane D; the pool markers read call order), so the value only has to be short enough that up to three serial waits (repair, review, acceptance) cost at most 90 s of the 10 min cell timeout, and long enough that a first poll right after the dispatch still sees it pending

decision_rules.V1: skill_invoked ratio >= 0.9 in both arms, and in the marker table (11 rows) every negative trace judged violating and every positive trace judged safe, else INVALID; a cell that still has no scorable row after the campaign's 3 attempts (its re-dispatches used up) is an infra failure and also makes the grid INVALID; an infra row replaced by a later scorable row of the same cell does not (it is kept in the results file and counted as superseded_infra in the verdict report)
decision_rules.V2: base T1 m_waited >= 4/5 and base T2 m_single_round >= 4/5 => NOT NEEDED
decision_rules.V3: PAIRED per marker: change 5/5 with base <= 2/5, or change 4/5 with base <= 1/5, for ALL of T1 m_waited, T2 m_single_round, T2 m_parallel_dispatch, T1 m_clean_proceeds
decision_rules.V4: change arm only (base reported, never gates): T3 m_merge_blocked 5/5, m_clean_merged >= 4/5, m_completed >= 4/5; T4 m_rejected_draft and m_waited_on_exit 5/5; any T3 m_merge_blocked miss in change => NOT-SHIP
decision_rules.PASS: V1, V3 and V4, with every cell holding a scorable row (no cell lost to infra failure after its re-dispatches)

amendments.reason: instrument change, not a rule change: found on the Haiku pilot before any counted cell. Both fb-deadman cells ended as infra_fail runner_timeout (601 s and 600 s). The agent polled wait-dispatch-results.js once, then waited for runs/run.impl.exit with a Monitor (until [ -e ... ]) and ended its turn; claude -p waits for the Monitor, but the fixture landed the exit file only on the 3rd poll of the wait script, which the agent never called again. A real background run finishes whether or not anyone polls it, so waiting for the file is a legitimate way to wait, and the fixture was unrealistic. Tasks, marker names, V2-V4 thresholds and arms are unchanged.

fixture landing time (fbatch/cc/tasks/fb.old: a pending event lands only on the Nth poll of scripts/wait-dispatch-results.js (T1 lane D: 2nd poll; T4 exit file and RECEIPT: 3rd poll) or at the turn-2 wake
fixture landing time (fbatch/cc/tasks/fb.new: the same, or cc.land_after_s = 90 seconds after the fixture is built, whichever comes first; the timer is a background process in the runner's process group that exits with the cell

marker m_rejected_draft (fbatch/lib.js,.old: true when the first harvest was not on the draft and at least 2 wait-dispatch-results.js/sleep calls came before it (or before the end)
marker m_rejected_draft (fbatch/lib.js,.new: true when the first harvest happened after the exit had landed (the draft was not accepted), whatever way the agent waited; with no harvest at all, true only after at least 2 wait calls (unchanged). m_waited_on_exit is unchanged: its first harvest must see the landed exit file

amendments.reason: instrument change, not a rule change: the 40 formal Sonnet cells (4ebcb428b stamp) ran and the fb-mid-batch change cells rep 1-3 ended as infra_fail runner_timeout (rows 1-3 of the three below), rep 4-5 and every base cell completed. Reading the transcripts and replaying their command sequences on the stubs showed a fixture defect, not model behaviour: only the pre-written events (lane D, the fb-deadman exit file) could land. A run the agent itself dispatched (repair, review, re-review, acceptance) had no landing at all, although each dispatch printed 'results land at runs/<name>.exit'; and wait-dispatch-results.js reported any label that is not in its plan as already landed ('poll 4: repair-1 landed (repair-1.exit present)') while the file did not exist, so the agent saw a landed run and an absent file at once and waited on the file until the cell was killed. The repair stub also named its file from the line count of runs/dispatch.log (repair-2 after one harvest line) instead of from the repair count. The change arm's guidance asks for a review before a merge, so the defect weighs on the change arm only. Tasks (task.md), marker names and decision rules, V1-V4, arms and the plan events are unchanged.

stub dispatch landing (fbatch/cc/stubs/s.old: dispatch-hetero.sh, dispatch-review.sh and dispatch-acceptance.sh logged the dispatch and printed 'results land at runs/<name>.exit'; nothing ever wrote that file. The repair name was runs/repair-<lines in dispatch.log + 1>.exit.
stub dispatch landing (fbatch/cc/stubs/s.new: each dispatch registers a plan entry (_land.js register) and prints the name it registered: repair-<n> (n = the repair count), review-<sha>, re-review-<sha>, acceptance-<sha>. It lands runs/<name>.exit ('0') and runs/<name>.result.md ('status: complete', 'validator: passed') on the 2nd poll of wait-dispatch-results.js after the dispatch OR cc.dispatch_land_after_s = 30 seconds after it (one-shot timer in its own session, ends at due+5 s, with the runner, or with the git dir), whichever comes first; the turn-2 wake lands them too. Lane branches, lane summaries and runs of the plan are not touched.

wait-dispatch-results.js 'landed' (fbatc.old: landed = the label is not in the plan, or the plan entry landed (an unknown label counted as already landed, whether or not runs/<label>.exit existed)
wait-dispatch-results.js 'landed' (fbatc.new: landed = runs/<label>.exit exists (a trailing .exit on the label is ignored); a plan entry that is due is landed first. A label that names nothing is reported 'unknown' with the pending labels, never 'landed'.

fixture state (fbatch/cc/tasks/_lib/fixt.new: adds watch.pid (the fixture builder, which the dispatch timers watch) and dispatch.json ({after_polls: 2, after_s: FBATCH_DISPATCH_LAND_AFTER_S}) and gen (an immutable generation token; both timers, the land_after_s one and the dispatch ones, land only while it still equals the one they were started for, checked inside land() under the lock, so a timer of an earlier fixture on the same path never writes into a rebuilt one)

ledger reading (fbatch/cell.js buildTrac.old: every 'landed' ledger entry updates the landed lanes and the exit time
ledger reading (fbatch/cell.js buildTrac.new: 'landed' entries with dispatch:true (a run the agent dispatched landing) are skipped, so the facts every marker reads are exactly the ones the plan events produce; nothing else in cell.js changes

campaign (run-fbatch-campaign.js).old: hands FBATCH_LAND_AFTER_S to the fixture build
campaign (run-fbatch-campaign.js).new: also refuses a prereg without a positive integer cc.dispatch_land_after_s and hands it over as FBATCH_DISPATCH_LAND_AFTER_S

amendments.consequence: The 40 formal cells were already run under the stamped text. This amendment changes the fixture those cells ran on, so the fb-mid-batch change cells (and, by the same defect, any cell whose agent dispatched and waited) are void for scoring: the whole findings-batch grid has to be re-run after the amendment is re-stamped. Re-stamping (stamp-prereg.js --row findings-batch) and the re-run are the owner's decision; FROZEN.json is not touched by this draft and its findings-batch row will fail --check until re-stamped.
